In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis, characterization, and supramolecular assembly of a novel class of optically active, helical PPEa's bearing oligo(ethylene oxide) side chains connected by amide groups to the polymer backbone.
the design and synthesis of a new family of helical PPEa's, which are optically active, self-assembling, and biodegradable, and thus may have potential as functional materials for nanotechnology.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PPEa's are optically active, amphipathic polymers that exhibit a stable helical structure in the solid state, in the bulk, and in solution, and that this helical structure is directly observable by AFM.
the helical structure is stabilized in solution by the hydrogen bonding, in the bulk by the amphiphilicity, and in the crystalline state by the combination of both.
the combination of an amphiphilic side chain and an intramolecular H-bonding motif is an efficient strategy to stabilize a helical conformation in PPEa's, even in nonpolar organic media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel class of helical polymers, PPEa, which are optically active and amphiphilic, and have been characterized by a wide variety of methods including X-ray crystallography, circular dichroism, UV/vis, NMR spectroscopy, and atomic force microscopy.
a combination of an intramolecular H-bonding network and a hydrophobic core in the side chain can be used to enforce helicity in PPEa and to control the absolute helical sense of the polymers.

the combination of an optically active, π-conjugated backbone and an amphiphilic side chain with a hydrogen-bonding motif provides a powerful approach for controlling and stabilizing the helical structure of a polymer and for visualizing its helical structures in the solid state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of an intramolecularly hydrogen-bonding amide group and an appropriate amphiphilic side chain can be used to enforce the helical conformation of a π-conjugated polymer and stabilize it even in the bulk.
the hydrogen-bonding interaction between the pendants is crucial for the formation of helical structures and the stabilization of the one-handed helical conformations of the main chains.
